dek: Set for 25 October 2026 at Dataran Tanjung Emas in Muar, Johor, this single-distance half marathon crosses Muar iconic twin bridges spanning the Muar River. Registration open. A distinctive Johor road race where two bridges and the post-race otak-otak define the experience.
verdict: The Twin Bridges Half Marathon Muar makes its course the star: a single-distance 21.1K route across Muar two bridges the Sultan Ismail Bridge (1967) and the Muar Second Bridge spanning the Muar River, starting and finishing at Dataran Tanjung Emas, the town waterfront esplanade. Registration is open. Muar is Johor royal town, known for its heritage architecture, its celebrated food scene, and its laid-back riverside character. October in Johor is the inter-monsoon period with warm, humid conditions and a moderate chance of afternoon thunderstorms that rarely trouble a morning start. The race online footprint is thin, with the Checkpoint Spot Asia listing as the primary public information source. For runners wanting a distinctive Johor bridge half marathon with open registration and Muar post-race food scene, this is a solid, bookable pick for 25 October 2026.

paragraphs: Muar two bridges spanning the Muar River the Sultan Ismail Bridge (opened 1967, the old bridge) and the Muar Second Bridge (the new bypass) provide a distinctive tandem crossing that gives the race its name. The bridges are the defining course feature: a 21.1K route that takes runners across both structures, with the Muar River below and the Straits of Malacca on the horizon. A bridge-centred half marathon is rare in the Malaysian calendar [1].
sections.heading: The Twin Bridges: Muar River Landmarks

paragraphs: Dataran Tanjung Emas is Muar waterfront esplanade, a popular local running spot with river views, sea breezes, and a central location in Muar town. As a race hub, it provides assembly space, parking, and the scenic backdrop of the Muar River meeting the Straits of Malacca. The single-distance format (21.1K only) keeps the race focused and the start-line energy unified [1].
sections.heading: Dataran Tanjung Emas: Muar Waterfront Start

paragraphs: Muar is Johor royal town, known for its heritage architecture, its celebrated food scene (Muar otak-otak and mee bandung are the local signatures), and its laid-back riverside character. For runners making the trip to Muar, the town offers a distinctive post-race experience: heritage shophouse coffee shops, the Sultan Ibrahim Jamek Mosque, and the Tanjung Emas waterfront at sunset. Muar is roughly 2 hours from KL and 45 minutes from Melaka [1][2].
sections.heading: Muar: Johor Royal Town

paragraphs: The course starts at Dataran Tanjung Emas, crosses both the Sultan Ismail Bridge and the Muar Second Bridge, and returns to the waterfront esplanade for the finish. The terrain is flat Muar sits on the Johor coastal plain and the bridges are engineered for minimal gradient. The dual-bridge crossing is a distinctive racing experience: two bridge decks, two different vantage points over the Muar River, and the open-water views of the Straits of Malacca [1].
sections.heading: The Course: Single-Distance Across Two Bridges

paragraphs: October sits in the inter-monsoon window, with morning temperatures of 25-28C, humidity around 80-85 percent, and a moderate chance of afternoon thunderstorms [3]. The Muar coastal location provides some breeze off the Straits of Malacca, but the bridge sections are elevated and exposed to wind. Morning starts benefit from cooler pre-dawn temperatures and the flat course profile aids heat management [3].
sections.heading: October in Johor: Inter-Monsoon

paragraphs: If you are a runner in Johor, Melaka, or southern KL who wants a distinctive bridge half marathon with open registration, a single-distance format, and Muar post-race food scene, the Twin Bridges Half Marathon is a solid pick for 25 October 2026. The dual-bridge course is unique in Malaysia, and the open registration window means you can book now [1].
